name: Mags Quire
title: of the Bindery
why: Just outside the north gate, where the first crack opened. She came from the Bindery to look at the seam.
examine: Mags Quire wears a very small spaceship badge. She has not explained it.
She carries a laser-awl in a holster and a ledger under one arm. The ledger is older than the road.
She counts things as she passes them. So far today, forty trees.
meet: Mags Quire, the Bindery. I got your paper bird. It was folded wrong.
You closed a rift. I counted it. That makes one.

wary: State your business. Keep it short.
neutral: You’re back. Good. I have a list.
warm: I saved you a place in the ledger. It’s a small place.
fond: I’ve put you down as crew. Don’t make me cross it out.

tired: That’s three items. I stop at three. Come back tomorrow.
finished: The list is empty. I don’t trust an empty list. I’ll write a new one.

say: This is a laser-awl. It mends seams. I was issued it sixty years ago and nobody has asked for it back.

options.text: How does it mend a seam?
reply: You find the thread and pull gently. The awl does the hot part.

options.text: Sixty years is a long time to keep a tool.
reply: It is. I’ve kept the receipt as well.
It’s cleaned on Thursdays. Today isn’t Thursday.

say: I fell through a rift in the middle of an inventory. I was on crate nine hundred and four. I still don’t know what was in nine hundred and five.

reply: No. I’ve made my peace with it. Mostly on Thursdays.

options.text: What was in nine hundred and four?
reply: Spoons. Two hundred of them. All first spoons.
It was inconvenient. I hadn’t initialled the page.

options.text: I could help you look for it.
reply: No. The ship is in another book. I don’t take favours. I issue them.

say: Rule one about strays. They’re more lost than you are. Rule two. Offer tea.

reply: Some of them do. Offer tea anyway. Stand back while you do it.

options.text: What if I don’t have tea?

say: People ask about the badge. It’s my ship. The real one was a great deal larger.

reply: The Quire. I was named after the job. So was the ship.
It’s to scale. A very small scale.

memories.asked-about-the-awl: You asked how the laser-awl mends a seam. She told you. She doesn’t tell everyone.
memories.crate-905: You said she will never know what was in crate nine hundred and five. She agreed.
memories.offer-tea-anyway: You said some strays bite. She said to offer tea anyway.
memories.the-ship: You said she misses her ship. She has logged it.

never: No. The Bindery needs a quartermaster, and that’s me. I’ll visit. I’ll bring my own cup.
camp.role: Visits, and brings her own cup.

wants.now: A full count of the first seam.
wants.really: To know what was in crate nine hundred and five.

sheet.opensUp: A question about how a tool works.

voice.hello: States what is on the list.

birch: A log. I’ll enter it as one log.
ash: Ash. I’ve logged it as one.
pine: Pine. It’s sticky. I’m not putting it near the ledger.
minnow: A fish. The Bindery has no line for fish. I’ll add one.
trout: A trout. It goes under fish. There’s a line for that now.
berries: Berries. I counted them. Forty. You ate one on the way.
herbs: Herbs. That’s tea. Rule two is covered.
stone: A stone. I have forty trees and one stone. Good.
copper: Copper. The awl takes copper wire. This saves me a requisition.

day.morning: Mornings I count the seam. It’s the same length. I count it anyway.
day.afternoon: Afternoons I write it up. Nobody reads it. It’s filed correctly.
day.evening: It’s late. The ledger closes at dusk. I’m still here. That goes in tomorrow.
day.night: I don’t sleep on a watch. I’ve logged this as rest.
day.rain: Rain. The ledger’s under my coat. The coat leaks. The ledger doesn’t.

wendell: The man in the road. He measures. I count. We don’t compare.
gorrin: I counted his cabbages. I got a third number. He took it well.
jonas: Two spoons. I told him about crate nine hundred and four. He sat down.

asked-about-the-awl: The awl’s been cleaned. It was Thursday.
crate-905: I thought about crate nine hundred and five again. Still nothing.
offer-tea-anyway: I offered a stray tea yesterday. It bit the cup. I’d stood back.
the-ship: I looked at the badge this morning. It’s still to scale.

arc.complication: A crate she will never open.
arc.kindness: Someone says she misses her ship.
